extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and legal professionals involved in reciprocal disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Model and requirements for imposing reciprocal exclusion from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 when a practitioner is disciplined by a state authority; includes service procedures, respondent rights, scope of exclusion, administrative notices, and post-exclusion duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) (state disbarment as predicate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion was ordered for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being disbarred from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the Supreme Court of California's disbarment of the respondent as the predicate. The state disbarment supports a USPTO finding under §11.804(h) and can serve as the basis for reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Notice and Order (mail and publication per 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director attempted service by certified first-class mail to addresses provided by the respondent; when the mailed Notice and Order was returned as 'Return to Sender', service was effected by publication in the Official Gazette for two consecutive weeks pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order records mailing tracking numbers, the Official Gazette issues (Aug 8 and Aug 15, 2017), and that the publication informed the respondent how to obtain a copy by request to the General Counsel. Use of publication under §11.35(b) is an accepted alternative when direct mail is undeliverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond and grounds to oppose (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent had an opportunity to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes the respondent did not file a response. The availability of specified defenses under §11.24(d)(1) is a required procedural safeguard; failure to respond may foreclose raising those defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: No genuine issue of material fact standard (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of the respondent's failure to file a response, the Director determined there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and that exclusion is the appropriate discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A default or lack of opposition permits the Director to conclude absence of a material factual dispute and to enter reciprocal discipline without further factual contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and effect of exclusion ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO, effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order implements exclusion as the disciplinary sanction; the scope mirrors practice before the USPTO across patent, trademark and other non-patent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette publication content (Notice of Exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is directed to publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Exclusion' text identifying the respondent, registration number, the violation (37 C.F.R. §11.804(h)), and the predicate state disbarment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order supplies sample notice text including mention of the state court's reason (failure to cooperate), the statutory authority (35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.24), and a pointer to OED's FOIA Reading Room for disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative dissemination to other jurisdictions and courts is required so that state and federal entities are informed of the USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of excluded practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order references §11.58 as imposing specific obligations on an excluded practitioner (the Order does not reproduce those duties), so compliance with that regulation is mandatory during exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ('PKI') certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/technical measures (dissociation of accounts and PKI credentials) are ordered to prevent the excluded person from practicing through existing customer numbers or certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall he have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative prohibition preventing the excluded person from circumvention by obtaining new or shared customer numbers until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions (OED FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs readers to the FOIA Reading Room for access to prior disciplinary decisions and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of state disbarment cited (failure to cooperate with disciplinary investigation / California Bus. & Prof. Code §6068)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court of California disbarred the respondent after his default for failing to respond to a notice of disciplinary charges; the charges addressed failure to cooperate with a State Bar disciplinary investigation, a violation of Section 6068 of the California Business and Professions Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explains the factual/legal basis of the predicate state discipline (failure to cooperate), which supports the USPTO's reciprocal determination under §11.804(h).
